stage: test_time_scaling / E7 test-time scaling (1 seed, K=8, 210-struct composition-exclusion, 416-eff matched to training)
prereg: prereg.md, committed before any E7 inference

generations.note: generated ONCE; every row scored offline from the SAME samples, so row differences are the selection rule, not sampling luck

effective_resolution.why: matched to training per the resolution_audit train/test mismatch artifact

H7a.rule: a deployable row beats D1 majority by >0.05 acc OR >10% relative AURC
H7a.interpretation: not a near miss — filtering by self-consistency is WORSE than not filtering. calibration's AUC 0.81 used the answer-independent geometry step scored AGAINST CIF TRUTH; D2/D3 have no truth and can only ask whether the model's emitted numbers match its own claim. A chain that FABRICATES a clean lattice and reasons correctly from it is maximally self-consistent AND wrong, so self-consistency preferentially selects confident fabrications. => the checker's predictive power is REAL but ORACLE-ONLY.

H7b.interpretation: accuracy clears the bar comfortably (0.912 vs 0.80) but coverage misses badly (0.16 vs 0.50). When the chain AGREES with the direct answer that answer is right 91% of the time vs 62% unconditionally, a +29pp lift — the chain is a good certifier on the slice it can certify, and that slice is small because the chain's own 0.38 accuracy bounds how often it agrees with a correct answer.

V2b.reading: ceiling nearly saturated — the chain's problem is GENERATION, not selection

B1.reading: large unrealised headroom; note O1 truth-rerank is WORSE than majority for B1 (0.5857 vs 0.6190) because a direct answer contains no geometry to score — null by construction, not a finding

bug_caught: the first scoring pass reported D3 with a plausible number, but enrichment metadata showed spglib_resolved=0/1680: spglib and pymatgen are NOT in the box's VLM env and a bare except silently turned every failure into 'no result', degenerating D3 into majority vote. Recomputed locally (spglib 2.7.0) where it resolves 1680/1680. LESSON: a fallback path must be counted and surfaced, never silent.
caveats: the certify-coverage limit is bounded by the chain's own 0.38 accuracy; a stronger chain would widen it — hypothesis, not result

post_hoc_stratified_certification.status: EXPLORATORY — designed after H7b failed; survives its control but must be pre-registered and re-run on the 3-seed matrix before being stated as a finding
post_hoc_stratified_certification.question: is the 91%-accurate certified slice merely the easy structures B1 would get right anyway?

aggregate_control.why_misleading: identical accuracy suggests the chain adds nothing, but the two selections share only 7 of 34 structures — same accuracy on largely DIFFERENT structures. B1's K=8 vote confidence takes only 6 values with 82/210 tied at 1.0, so a top-k cut is mostly an arbitrary tie-break, not a ranking.

post_hoc_stratified_certification.headline: chain agreement carries correctness information BEYOND the answerer's own confidence. Among the 82 structures where B1 is UNANIMOUS across all 8 samples it is right 70.1% alone but 100% (15/15) when the verified chain independently agrees — self-consistency cannot separate those cases, an independently-derived chain can.
post_hoc_stratified_certification.does_not_change: H7b still FAILS (rule required acc>=0.80 AT coverage>=0.5; coverage is 0.16). This explains why the certified slice is good; it does not rescue the hypothesis.
